reference: Bash type/help verify metadata. Offline operation contracts use hand-encoded RFC 1035 zone/message fixtures and the documented chain/checkzone/doh-codec output API. No network or GNU dig/drill equivalence is claimed.
coverage: Bash builtin classification for the statically installed dns loadable.
Short description, synopsis, and documented command-family metadata exposed by Bash help.
Deferred operation coverage is scoped to DNS query transports, client updates, and local resolver/authoritative service exchanges.
Offline parent-chain calculation, valid/inherited-owner and invalid-address master-file parsing, and a fixed in-memory DoH POST decoder contract.
DoT transport retries: timeouts use every resolver attempt, while a failed handshake or verification is final.
Transport settings assigned for a single dns command reach the DoT and DoH children intact.
exclusions: All network exchanges, listener/service operations, transfers and polling remain deferred; offline parser/codec cases do not establish network parity.
Signing, credentials and trust-anchor management are unexecuted. Broader offline parser/codec conformance remains a gap.

cases.purpose: GNU Bash type -t reports a loaded Bash builtin as builtin. This confirms availability metadata without invoking dns.
Bash help -d exposes the documented DNS command description; metadata only.
Bash help -s exposes the documented public query synopsis; metadata only.
cases.stdout: dns: dns A|AAAA|MX|TXT|... HOST [-s SERVER] [-t TIMEOUT_MS] [-d] [--validate] [--skew SEC]

cases.purpose: The complete help text retains stable documentation for the master-file checker, authoritative server, and DNSSEC features; checks only Bash metadata and does not run those commands.
Exercise DNS query construction, response parsing, common RR presentation, error responses, resolver search order, and TC-triggered TCP fallback.
Exercise DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS framing, certificate validation, and DNS message handling through each transport.
Exercise RFC 2136 update and RFC 1996 notify requests, prerequisite encodings, TSIG signing, and peer response validation.
Exercise authoritative UDP/TCP answers, zone selection, transfer/update policy, TSIG, and opt-in service features against clients.
Exercise resolver forwarding/cache behavior and the documented recursive, DNSSEC, DNS64, and policy paths against controlled peers.
Exercise slave IXFR/AXFR transfer verification and DNSKEY polling used by trust-anchor rollover.
Compute the documented parent-domain chain as a pure text operation without DNS resolution.
Validate a small RFC 1035 zone including an inherited owner and documented serial reporting; addresses are text only.
cases.script:
cat > zone <<'ZONE'
$ORIGIN example.test.
$TTL 300
@ IN SOA ns.example.test. hostmaster.example.test. 2026010101 3600 600 86400 300
@ IN NS ns.example.test.
ns IN A 192.0.2.1
www IN A 192.0.2.2
    IN AAAA 2001:db8::2
ZONE
dns checkzone -o example.test. zone

A DoT child stopped after the query timeout is transient and is retried for each configured resolver attempt; a child that exits non-zero by itself (a failed handshake or verification) ends the attempts. A test stub replaces the TLS transport and counts its invocations.
cases.script:
printf 'nameserver 127.0.0.1\noptions attempts:3\n' > resolv
export BASHDNS_RESOLV_CONF=$PWD/resolv PATH=/usr/bin:/bin
for stub in timeout failure; do
  : > calls
  if [[ $stub == timeout ]]; then
    export BASHDNS_DOT_CMD='printf x >> calls; sleep 5'
  else
    export BASHDNS_DOT_CMD='printf x >> calls; exit 1'
  fi
  rc=0
  dns query example.com A -t 300 --dot -h 127.0.0.1 2>/dev/null || rc=$?
  n=$(<calls)
  printf '%s status=%s calls=%s\n' "$stub" "$rc" "${#n}"
done
cases.stdout:
timeout status=1 calls=3
failure status=1 calls=1

cases.purpose: Transport settings given as assignments for the single dns command (with PATH also assigned there) reach the DoT and DoH children intact. Bash frees its shared getenv buffer for such assignments at the next lookup, which the child's PATH search makes before running the command. A test stub records which transport command ran.
cases.script:
printf 'nameserver 127.0.0.1\n' > resolv
for mode in dot doh dot-env; do
  : > seen
  rc=0
  case $mode in
    dot) BASHDNS_RESOLV_CONF=$PWD/resolv BASHDNS_DOT_CMD='printf dot > seen; exit 1' PATH=/usr/bin:/bin dns query example.com A -t 300 --dot -h 127.0.0.1 2>/dev/null || rc=$? ;;
    doh) BASHDNS_RESOLV_CONF=$PWD/resolv BASHDNS_DOH_CMD='printf doh > seen; exit 1' PATH=/usr/bin:/bin dns query example.com A -t 300 --doh https://127.0.0.1/dns-query 2>/dev/null || rc=$? ;;
    dot-env) BASHDNS_RESOLV_CONF=$PWD/resolv BASHDNS_DOT=1 BASHDNS_DOT_HOST=127.0.0.1 BASHDNS_DOT_CMD='printf dot-env > seen; exit 1' PATH=/usr/bin:/bin dns query example.com A -t 300 2>/dev/null || rc=$? ;;
  esac
  printf '%s status=%s seen=%s\n' "$mode" "$rc" "$(<seen)"
done
cases.stdout:
dot status=1 seen=dot
doh status=1 seen=doh
dot-env status=1 seen=dot-env
